questions.question_text: Which event is generally considered the turning point (Milestone) in the life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) that marked the beginning of the Islamic calendar (AH)?
options: The receiving of the first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq) in the Cave Hira
The Hijra (Migration) from Makkah to Madinah
The establishment of the first Islamic community (Ummah) in Madinah
questions.explanation: The Hijra marked the migration to Madinah, leading to the start of the Islamic calendar in 622 CE.

questions.question_text: During which period did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) focus primarily on developing the social and political structure of the nascent Muslim community in Madinah?
options: The early years after the Hijra (establishing the Constitution of Madinah)
The period of revelation in Makkah (before Hijra)
questions.explanation: The early years in Madinah involved crafting the Constitution of Madinah (Sahifat al-Madinah) to establish societal order and rights.

questions.question_text: Which pillar of Islam mandates the giving of a fixed portion of one's wealth to the needy, and is considered a purification of wealth?
questions.explanation: Zakat is the mandatory charity calculated on accumulated wealth, ensuring socio-economic balance.

questions.question_text: Which significant event during Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) early life marks his reputation as a man of honesty and trust?
options: Being entrusted with the management of the Kaaba keys.
Successfully mediating a dispute between tribal leaders.
His involvement in the trade caravan to Syria.
Passing the test of sacrifice during the Kaaba's rebuilding.
questions.explanation: His honesty and trustworthy character earned him the title 'Al-Amin' (The Trustworthy), which was evident during his trade journeys.

questions.question_text: If a person is physically unable to perform the Hajj journey, what is the acceptable alternative prescribed by Islamic law?
options: Making a formal pledge (Nazar) to pray extra prayers
questions.explanation: Compensation (Fidya) through sacrifice or fasting is required for those who cannot physically complete the Hajj due to genuine inability.

questions.question_text: Which pillar of Islam mandates the annual payment of a fixed sum of money on the shoulders of ability, calculated from accumulated wealth?
questions.explanation: Zakat is the obligatory charity paid on wealth that has reached a minimum threshold (Nisab) and has been held for a specific time.

questions.question_text: Which event marked the beginning of Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) prophetic mission (Nubuwwat) and divine revelation?
options: The marriage to Khadijah bint Khuwaylid.
The construction of the Kaaba in the pre-Islamic era.
The revelation of the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq in the Cave Hira.
questions.explanation: The start of the prophethood occurred in the Cave Hira when the first divine revelation (Iqra) was received.
